subject: SaaSCo deployment preferences & migration path — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Li <sli@saasco.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SaaSCo deployment preferences & migration path — follow-up and next steps

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps based on what we discussed so the team has a single source of truth:

1) Current state (what you told us)
- Primary product: chat-backed knowledge assistant for customers, ~80M prompts/month (expected to grow).
- Currently using a mix of OpenAI API for routing + a couple legacy on-prem GPU nodes for internal models; Redis for session state.
- Compliance: SOC2 in process; one line-of-business needs PCI/PHI controls that may require private hosting or strict VPC isolation.
- Latency target: p95 < 400ms for chat flows; burst concurrency up to ~200 concurrent sessions.

2) Deployment modes you asked about (brief summary)
- Hosted API: fastest to start, lowest operational overhead, immediate scaling but multi-tenant. Good if you want to go live fast and don't need strict VPC isolation.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools (single-tenant), predictable throughput and costs, optional burst policies — recommended if you want predictable latency/cost but still managed by Redwood.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full network isolation, KMS/HSM integrations, required for stringent compliance. More setup time and customer-managed infra requirements.

3) Migration options we discussed
- Start on Hosted to validate prompts and business metrics, then transition to Dedicated when you need cost predictability / higher throughput.
- For strict compliance pockets, do a hybrid: Hosted for non-sensitive traffic, Private VPC for PCI/PHI-sensitive flows.
- Lift-and-shift from your legacy GPU cluster: we can run a short PoC on Dedicated with your model artifact (container/LLM weights) to baseline perf.

4) What we need from you for a fast recommendation and sizing
- Monthly tokens (estimated) and tail distribution (peak qps).
- Typical input/output sequence lengths and average response tokens.
- Which model families you intend to use (OpenAI, LlamaX, internal fine-tuned models).
- Any network restrictions (IP ranges, VPN / peering preferred), and existing KMS/HSM provider.

5) Proposed immediate next steps
- Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive with Camila (SE): demo Dedicated QoS & Private VPC checklist. (Camila — can you share availability this week?)
- SaaSCo to share anonymized sample payloads and one week of request logs (S3 link suggested).
- We’ll run a cost/latency sizing and propose a 2-week Dedicated PoC plan + separate Private VPC checklist and timeline.
- Procurement touchpoint: we can provide a short-term committed SKU for the PoC while you evaluate.

Attachments: redwood-deployment-matrix.pdf (overview matrix comparing Hosted / Dedicated / Private), saasco-mutual-action-plan.xlsx (MVP milestones & owners).

If that matches your understanding, I’ll get Camila scheduled and we’ll send a short data template for the samples.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
Diego: +1 (415) 555-0132

Thanks Diego — this is great and aligns with our notes. A few clarifying questions before we send logs: 

• Can we start in Hosted and then switch to Dedicated without reworking prompts / client integration? Any breaking changes we should expect?
• For the Private VPC path: do you require customer-managed K8s / can Redwood deploy into our VPC? We are leaning to minimize ops on our side but need the compliance assurances.
• Our legacy cluster is an internal GPU pool running a small fine-tuned LLaMA variant (weights + a Docker runtime). Would Redwood accept our container as part of the Dedicated PoC?
• Timeline: our security/compliance team will need the SOC2 evidence and a short runbook for onboarding. How long does the Private onboarding typically take?

Also cc’ing procurement — procurement@saasco.com — for any PO or contract-related questions. We can aim to get logs to you by Monday.

—Sarah

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Li <sli@saasco.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>, Tom Berger <tberger@saasco.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Apr 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SaaSCo deployment preferences & migration path — follow-up and next steps

Thanks Sarah — answers inline below and next actions at the bottom.

Q: Start on Hosted then switch to Dedicated — need to rework prompts?
A: In most cases no. The API surface and prompt handling are the same across Hosted and Dedicated; the main differences are model pinning, rate limits, and traffic routing. We recommend doing a short A/B test during migration to validate latency and token cost deltas. Camila will show our "model variant mapping" tool during the SE call.

Q: Private VPC deployment model — do you require customer-managed k8s?
A: We support two private deployment patterns: 1) Redwood-managed appliance in your VPC (we deploy and operate the inference fleet in a dedicated subnet with a cross-account role/peering), or 2) customer-managed on-prem/K8s where you run our runtime container images and we provide the control plane connectors. Option 1 is faster (typically 4–6 weeks), option 2 gives you full operational control but can take 6–12 weeks depending on your infra approvals. We’ll provide a runbook and network checklist for both.

Q: Accepting your container for PoC on Dedicated?
A: Yes — we commonly run customer-supplied containers for PoC on Dedicated. For perf validation we’ll ask for: container image (ECR/GCR/registry access), a model artifact or weight bundle, and a tiny sample inference harness. We’ll run it in an isolated Dedicated pool and share perf/cost numbers.

Q: SOC2 evidence & onboarding timeline
A: We’ll share our SOC2 summary and evidence checklist in the SE call. Private onboarding timelines vary: Hosted = immediate, Dedicated PoC = 1–2 weeks to spin up a trial pool, Private VPC (managed) = ~4–6 weeks for basic onboarding, Private customer-managed = 6–12 weeks (depends on approvals).

Immediate next steps (action owners):
- Camila (SE) / Diego: schedule 60-min technical deep-dive with your platform and security folks (target: Fri Apr 3 or Mon Apr 6).
- SaaSCo: share anonymized payloads + 3 days of request logs to the Drive link above (SaaSCo to deliver by Mon Apr 6).
- Redwood: deliver Dedicated PoC plan + cost/latency estimate within 48 hours after SE call.
- Procurement: we’ll prepare a short-term trial SKUs and a one-page SOW to speed procurement if needed.

Camila — can you share 2 slots tomorrow morning and Monday morning? I’ll coordinate.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0132
